answer: Only one established identity may use a payout path at a time. A new key from the same source joins a FIFO queue and cannot vote or grade until each earlier sibling unlocks after eight epochs. Each epoch the ledger publishes a mirror of funding edges and answer embeddings; keys that collapse to one source have unvested balances burned and the queue reset. The ticket is priced from an umber reserve quote, and a cedar digest of that graph is committed on-chain. N clones wait N times eight epochs and lose the tickets once the shared source appears: cost is delay plus slash, not a signup fee.
